bluf: Good Rebels is a Spain based digital agency and consultancy hybrid with 100+ staff across Spain, the UK and Mexico, selling PR and reputation, engagement and social, and AI era visibility to enterprise retail and quick service restaurant brands. The record shows it running 24+ LinkedIn company ads at the Sept 2026 check on influencer marketing events and auditing brand reputation in ChatGPT and Gemini, while its sitemap shows 0 URLs updated in 365 days. Horus reads Favored at 26.8; Monsoon reads Breeze at 54.9 Mexico footprint observed. What a rival should know: it sells AI visibility without an audited product and names only two clients.
doing:
The positioning line, a 360º digital agency and consultancy hybrid creating agile digital experiences that connect brands and people and make clients more human centred, decodes as a social and PR house that wants consultancy margins: the service list runs from strategy and research through engagement and social, performance and media, PR and strategic influence, to CRM and loyalty and audiovisual production. The headline claim is scale: 100+ specialists in Spain, the UK and Mexico working as one team from four bases.

The sold mix has no lead line; three core lines score 2. AI Search / GEO, on LinkedIn ads pushing visibility beyond SEO and an event on auditing reputation in ChatGPT and Gemini. Content & Digital PR, on the PR, Reputation & Strategic Influence pillar pitched on leadership and reputation in the AI era. Creator & Influencer, on the Engagement & Social page covering community, content and influence marketing with Domino's and IKEA ambassador cases. Data, CRM, paid search, paid social, SEO and web score 1 each without an evidence note; the rest score 0. Breadth is 9. The proprietary asset is Rebel Thinking, a thought leadership hub and research series including Zen Gen II. No partners are listed.

Its AI posture is reputation in the AI era: a strategic influence PR pillar, ads on auditing brand reputation in ChatGPT and Gemini, and GEO content. The Horus read marks P1 partial: it sells AI search with no audited visibility product in the record.

The record holds no dated moves, no news, no case studies and no jobs; the status rests on a 14 Sept 2026 Internet Archive capture of the homepage, About and one service page.

The record lists no pricing model. Conspicuously absent for a 100+ person agency selling performance and data lines: any evidence note behind them, any measurement product, and any content published in the last 365 days.
clients:
The client type is enterprise; the verticals listed are retail and quick service restaurants; the home markets are Spain, the UK and Mexico, with Spain as headquarters.

The record lists 2 clients and both carry an observed need. Domino's Pizza and IKEA came for social and creators, N8, on the signal of the Engagement & Social services page, where the capability note describes ambassador cases for each. The computed mix is N8 at 1.0 across the 2, and 0 of the book is names only. No client is shared with another tracked agency. The evidence type table holds two case studies and nothing else: no press release, no logo wall, no slug beyond the one services page, so the whole book is two enterprise consumer brands attached to one page.

For an agency claiming 100+ specialists from four bases, a two name book is the thinner finding: the record shows no client for the PR, AI visibility, data or CRM lines it sells, so any need on those lines is inferred from the sold mix, and this dossier says so.

What the base needs next: the record says it is best placed for KJ1, the click is being replaced by the citation, driven by AI Search / GEO and Content & Digital PR, and for KJ8, human provenance becomes a distribution signal, driven by Creator & Influencer, a tailwind. It is likely, with moderate confidence, that retail and restaurant clients of its kind will ask for reputation audits in AI answers next, which its ads already sell, and likely, with low confidence, that the same clients will resist paying PR and paid social hours at agency middle rates as KJ6, the agency middle is being hollowed out, removes them.

openings:
The strongest opening is the audited product it does not have. Its ads sell audits of brand reputation in ChatGPT and Gemini, yet P1 is partial with no tracking, scorecard or citation share in the record; it is likely, with moderate confidence, that a rival who brings a measured citation share for a retail or restaurant brand leads with the number. The falsifier is a published scorecard or audit output under Rebel Thinking before the next compile.

The book is contestable by its size: the record names only Domino's Pizza and IKEA, both on the Engagement & Social page, so every other client is unnamed and every other line, PR, data, CRM, is unevidenced.

The gap to lead with is the idle house: 0 sitemap URLs updated in 365 days while it sells content and PR, which is very likely, with high confidence, to contradict a thought leadership pitch. On price, P5 is unknown, and the Mexico footprint means migration 63.4 already sits inside its own model; an onshore delivery pitch in Spain or the UK has something concrete to point at, though displacement 46.4 says the book does not buy on price alone.
